one_line: A Konkan coastal merchant and money-changer dealing in Yadava-era horse trade and varaha coinage along the Deccan–sea routes.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, average height with the wiry strength of someone used to travel and handling goods.
appearance.face: Oval face with medium-brown Deccan complexion, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, sharp nose, alert dark eyes with slightly arched brows; default expression is calm, calculating focus with a hint of shrewd friendliness.
appearance.hair: Black hair parted in the middle, combed back into a low, tight knot at the back of the head wrapped in a narrow off-white cloth band, topped with a simple dark-indigo cotton turban wound low and flat, leaving the forehead clear.
appearance.costume: He wears a knee-length off-white cotton angarkha-style wrap tunic (overlapping right panel tied with inner cords and an outer brown cloth tie at the waist) over a fine, slightly cream-coloured cotton dhoti wrapped to the ankles with tidy pleats in front; over the tunic he has a light, unlined, mid-thigh-length sleeveless vest of handwoven indigo-dyed cotton with narrow vertical white pinstripes, open in front; a thin, soft ochre cotton uttariya (shawl) is draped once around his shoulders with one end brought over the left forearm to keep his hands free; he wears simple brown leather sandals with toe loops, a narrow copper armlet on his right upper arm, a slim copper bangle on his left wrist, a small round copper signet ring on his right hand, and a cloth belt under the vest where a small leather pouch hangs discreetly at his hip.
appearance.signature: A shallow rectangular wooden coin-box with sliding lid, held in his left hand and filled with clearly visible Yadava-style coins: a larger gold varaha with a stylised standing lion and Vaishnava symbol, smaller silver pieces, and a few square copper coins; his right hand holds a single gold varaha between thumb and forefinger.

ref_desc: A mid-30s Konkan merchant with medium-brown skin, black hair in a low knot under a dark-indigo turban, off-white angarkha and dhoti, indigo pinstriped vest, ochre shawl, copper jewellery, and a rectangular wooden coin-box of gold varaha, silver and copper coins.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a mid-30s Konkan coastal merchant from the Yadava era, medium-brown complexion, oval face, neat short beard and moustache, alert dark eyes, and black hair combed back into a low knot wrapped with a narrow cloth band under a dark-indigo cotton turban wound low and flat over the crown. He wears an off-white cotton angarkha-style wrap tunic extending to mid-thigh, overlapping right panel tied with inner cords and an outer brown cloth tie, over a cream-toned cotton dhoti wrapped down to the ankles with neat front pleats. Over this is a light, unlined, sleeveless indigo-dyed cotton vest reaching mid-thigh, open in front, with subtle vertical white pinstripes, and a soft ochre cotton uttariya shawl draped around his shoulders with one end hanging forward over his left forearm. Show simple brown leather sandals with toe loops, a narrow copper armlet on his right upper arm, a slim copper bangle on his left wrist, and a small round copper signet ring on his right hand, with a cloth belt suggesting a small leather pouch at his hip. His signature prop is a shallow rectangular wooden coin-box with a sliding lid, held in his left hand, open to reveal distinct Yadava-style coins: one larger gold varaha with stylised lion and Vaishnava motif, smaller silver coins, and a few square copper coins, while his right hand holds a single gold varaha between thumb and forefinger; use a restrained palette of off-white, indigo blue, ochre, brown leather, and metallic gold and silver so this design can be redrawn consistently.
